newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mob boss Joey "Doves" Aiuppa dies.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mob boss Joey "Doves" Aiuppa dies.

text.p: Joseph "Joey Doves" Aiuppa, a former head of the Chicago mafia and one-time bodyguard to mobster Al "Scarface" Capone, has died at age 89, a hospital spokeswoman said Sunday.
Aiuppa had suffered from throat cancer and heart disease for years. The spokeswoman for suburban Elmhurst Memorial Hospital did not give the cause of death, which occurred Saturday.

Aiuppa had lived in the Chicago area since his January 1996 release for medical reasons from a Minnesota prison hospital, where he was serving a 28-year sentence for skimming $2 million from Las Vegas casinos.

Originally an amateur boxer who fought his way out of Chicago's Maxwell Street ghetto, Aiuppa was hired by Capone to provide protection for Capone's bootlegging, gambling and prostitution rackets that thrived in the city during the 1920s Prohibition era.

He later served as second in command to mob boss Anthony "Big Tuna" Accardo, another former enforcer for Capone, and became the ruthless king of the mafia's midwestern operations until his 1986 conviction for skimming casino profits.
Upon his release from prison, mob watchers believed the still-wealthy Aiuppa became a consiglieri, or elder statesman, as had Accardo in his last days.
Aiuppa acquired his nickname "Doves" after federal wildlife agents arrested him in 1962 with hundreds of mourning doves in his car trunk.

Aiuppa and some fellow gangsters had returned from a Kansas hunting trip where they used shotguns to blast the doves from electricity lines. For that, the mob boss -- said to have ordered killings and beatings -- was given a three-month sentence.
